reviews.title: Don’t waste your money
reviews.text:
I purchased a lifetime membership for Strong, and I genuinely regret it.
Since purchasing, I've become increasingly disappointed with the app's lack of functionality and innovation. Compared to competitors like Hevy, Strong feels years behind.
There's no import functionality, no AI or ChatGPT integration, and no intelligent recommendations on when to increase weights or progressively overload. Ultimately, it feels like a glorified note-taking app rather than a modern strength-training platform.
I've contacted the developers directly, but their support has been incredibly disappointing. There are constant promises of improvements coming in the future, yet very little meaningful progress. Meanwhile, competitors continue to innovate and release new features.
I requested a refund for my lifetime membership, which was refused. I now feel stuck with a product that isn't keeping pace with the industry.
We're living in an era where technology, particularly AI, is advancing rapidly. Strong seems to be standing still.
I genuinely struggle to understand how this app maintains such a high rating. In its current state, I simply cannot recommend it, especially when better alternatives exist.
One star. I wish I could get my money back.

reviews.title: The workout app field is expanding rapidly and Strong is getting left behind.
reviews.text:
I’m quickly finding that there’s no perfect workout app. There’s always a these things are great or improvements over this app…but…and the “but” is the key because it comes down to which app is offering the trade offs you’re willing to live without? 

My frustration with Strong is we are still dealing with syncing issues between the Apple Watch and the iPhone. The whole purpose of starting and ending workouts on the Watch was supposed to be to minimize these issues yet I still find I’m having increasingly more issues with ghost workouts - workouts started and ended on Apple Watch but instead of syncing they go into workout purgatory only to show up after you log out and log back in. If this wasn’t as frequent as it occurs it may be something you could deal with occasionally but it’s not.

Secondly, when you create exercises, you’re unable to assign body parts to them after saving them initially. Even if you go to the exercise library and edit them there. Additionally there’s no way to add photos. I beta test a lot of workout apps and this is one place where people are smoking Strong. Here’s why this matters: Strong doesn’t have a lot of common gym exercises in the library. So when you create them that means they also won’t have images or instructions on how to do them. Meanwhile Strong is starting to feel very Windows XP in a Windows 11 world.  This is also seen in the charts and graphs which seem flat and dated versus many newer apps offer richer charts and data presentation

reviews.title: Used to be good
reviews.text: Little changes have been made that make no sense. Why can I take notes on a set of any given move, but when I view the history of that move I can’t see the notes? When I do a move on Wednesday, I can’t see the angle I used or changes I made from the last Friday. That USED to be possible, and I even emailed about it last year, but it’s still gone. That’s useless.

reviews.title: Illogical Workout Finish
reviews.text: There is no way to make skipped sets carry over to future workouts without losing other changes. You will see skipped exercises disappear or else newly added exercises disappear, depending on which of the 3 illogical “finish workout” options the app offers. Very frustrating. Difficult to maintain a consistent routine. People have been complaining about this for years on Reddit but it’s still not fixed.

reviews.title: No Longer Updating
reviews.text:
The app is good except for the fact that is seems like they've stopped caring or updating the app. 

The list of workouts in their database is extremely limited. You can add your own, but they don't allow you add any images/ videos/notes for reference. I think with ALL the apps out there, they should be updating their list of workouts weekly to include visuals and notes. Or at least let users upload their own videos/photos/notes when adding a new workout. 

I also think whenever you use a template for a workout, if you change it during your active workout and then finish - there should be a 3rd option to "Save As New" that doesn't alter your original template but allows you to save what you created as a whole new template. They only currently allow you to either keep your original template or override your original template.

reviews.title: Buggy and Unreliable
reviews.text:
I have used this app for years, although it is pretty good and collates all sorts of data into one place and is especially powerful for those interested in Powerlifting etc., the app has always been buggy, workouts not synchronising, workouts misalignment with iPhone and Apple Watch, workouts disappearing. 
These bugs have remained the same over more than 5 years of use and the developers haven’t bothered to fix them. It’s actually gotten worse where the app deletes workouts and won’t even synchronise between Watch and iPhone. I’ve had enough and won’t be renewing my subscription. 
Don’t waste your money if you hope to use an Apple Watch with this.
